title: Enticingly Crispy Korean Duck Legs Korean Fried Chicken
description: A malty, bouncy-qq, brunch-mood Korean dish featuring duck legs, this low-carb-friendly recipe is a twist on traditional Korean fried chicken, using duck legs instead of chicken for a richer flavor and crisper exterior.
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk together rice vinegar, gochujang, soy sauce, brown sugar, garlic, and ginger to make the brine.
Add the duck legs to the brine and refrigerate for at least 2 hours or overnight.
Preheat the oil in a deep frying pan to 375 degrees.
In a separate bowl, mix together the potato starch and a pinch of salt.
Remove the duck legs from the brine and coat in the potato starch mixture, shaking off excess.
Carefully add the coated duck legs to the hot oil and fry for 5-7 minutes on each side, or until golden brown and crispy.
Using a slotted spoon, remove the duck legs from the oil and place on a paper towel-lined plate to drain excess oil.
Serve the crispy duck legs hot and enjoy.
Garnish with toasted sesame seeds and chopped green onions, if desired.
